catalog_quote: 2.0 Tone (Tone marks: (’) high tone low tone (!) downstep. e.g. Kofi; ...). It has not been possible in this study to do a detailed tonal analysis of Brong. Moreover there are marked differences in the tonal patterns used in different parts of the Brong-speaking areas, and what follows is therefore a brief statement of some of the ways in which the Brong dialect cluster as a whole differs tonally from the Akuapem, Asante and Fante dialects. 2.1 The Emphatic Particle né The emphatic particle né is always said on a high tone. In the other Akan dialects it is a low tone na. ... 2.2 Possessive Noun Phrase with the Possessive ‘Pronoun’ In the following examples the possessive ‘pronoun’ in Brong, like in Fante, is said on a high tone, while it is said on a low tone in Akuapem and Asante. ... 2.3 Verbal Forms In the following examples, the Brong verbal forms differ tonally from one or more …

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation (Dolphyne 1979 sec. 2.0-2.3) is present verbatim in the held archive.org scanned text at the stated place, with foot folios 95/96 bracketing it exactly as the locator says; the sec. 1.21 'stress on the final syllable' diachronic aside is also where the record puts it (p. 91). (2) Deciding source: a 1979 31-page dialect sketch by Dolphyne; authoritative author, but the tone section is self-declared as not a tonal analysis. Identity is correct (Glottolog files this chapter under abro1238). (3) Better Bono/Abron-specific phonology exists and is not held: Bota 2002 MPhil 'Bono Phonology' (Glottolog-coded under [aka], so absent from our abro1238 ref list), Bota 2007 SLAVOB-4 article on the Bono tonal system (UGSpace metadata only), Kossonou 2015 524-pp grammar and Timyan-Ravenhill 1983 sketch for Ivorian Abron. sources.quote: None. Ethnography; only an orthographic note on Bono-Twi spellings and a remark that Techiman-Wenchi and Dormaa-Berekum Bono-Twi 'deviate considerably from Asante-Twi', deferring to Dolphyne's survey.
sources.locator: front-matter note on Bono-Twi orthography (scanned lines ~300-320) and dialect remarks (lines ~528-533); no occurrence of tone/tonal/accent/pitch in a linguistic sense anywhere in the text
